landmarks.text: Concrete on the facade is painted to imitate ornamental tile.
landmarks.q: What color are the tile medallions on the Superior Bathhouse facade?

landmarks.text: The brewery's own history says it opened in the Superior Bathhouse in 2013.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse now houses a brewery and distillery?

landmarks.text: EoA calls the Hale, built in 1892-93, the oldest surviving bathhouse; the Buckstaff (1912), Fordyce (1914-15) and Lamar (1923) came later.
landmarks.q: Which is the oldest surviving bathhouse on Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?

landmarks.text: Thompson, Sanders & Ginocchio's late-1930s remodel changed the facade from neo-Classical revival to Mission Style in 1939-40.
landmarks.q: In what architectural style was the Hale Bathhouse facade remodeled in 1939–40?

landmarks.text: The pool was installed in 1931 to treat paralysis; the Maurice was the only bathhouse to employ a registered physical therapist.
landmarks.q: What was the Maurice Bathhouse's 1931 therapeutic pool built for?

landmarks.text: The Fordyce reopened as the visitor center on May 13, 1989.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row building houses Hot Springs National Park's visitor center and museum?
landmarks.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Hot Springs National Park

landmarks.text: Its chevron-mosaic dome is topped by a small copper cupola.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse is crowned by a large tiled dome?

landmarks.text: Scalloped shells frame the sculpin, originally gold and now white.
landmarks.q: Which fish decorates the parapets of Hot Springs' Quapaw Bathhouse?

landmarks.text: The 1922 Spanish Colonial Revival design has a vague Art Deco look.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse has twin towers with three-tiered setbacks?

landmarks.text: NPS says the Buckstaff opened on February 1, 1912, and has been in continuous operation since.
landmarks.q: Which Bathhouse Row bathhouse has offered baths continuously since 1912?

landmarks.text: Cream brick with white stucco trim and brass "Buckstaff Baths" letters.
landmarks.q: What color is the brick of the Buckstaff Bathhouse?

landmarks.text: NPS: the final metamorphosis of Bathhouse Row was completed when the Lamar opened in 1923; it closed in 1985.
landmarks.q: Which bathhouse's 1923 opening completed Hot Springs' Bathhouse Row?

landmarks.text: Work began in the 1930s on the promenade behind the bathhouses, which was finally completed in the early 1960s.
landmarks.q: In what decade did construction begin on the Grand Promenade behind Bathhouse Row?

landmarks.text: The lattice steel observation tower was officially opened to the public on June 3, 1983.
landmarks.q: How tall is the Hot Springs Mountain Tower?

landmarks.text: Construction began in 1982; it opened June 3, 1983.
landmarks.q: In what month and year did the current Hot Springs Mountain Tower open?

landmarks.text: The steel Rix Tower, opened in 1906, had an elevator to carry visitors to the top.
landmarks.q: What was the steel observation tower that preceded today's Hot Springs Mountain Tower called?

landmarks.text: The USGS says the park is best known for its 47 hot springs, which emerge from Hot Springs Mountain at an average temperature of 143 degrees Fahrenheit.
landmarks.q: According to the USGS, how many hot springs emerge from Hot Springs Mountain in Hot Springs National Park?

landmarks.text: NPS calls the Hot Springs thermal springs the hottest east of the Rocky Mountains, and says they average 143 degrees Fahrenheit.
landmarks.q: NPS calls the Hot Springs thermal springs the hottest east of what landmark?

landmarks.text: NPS says the Hot Springs thermal springs produce over 700,000 gallons of water a day.
landmarks.q: Per the National Park Service, about how much water do the Hot Springs thermal springs produce per day?

landmarks.text: Hot Springs has had three successive Arlington Hotel buildings, dating from 1875, 1892–93 and 1924.
landmarks.q: How many successive Arlington Hotel buildings has Hot Springs had?

landmarks.text: The 1893 Arlington had 300 rooms, but only 50 had their own baths. It burned in 1923.
landmarks.q: How many of the second Arlington Hotel's 300 guest rooms had private bathrooms?

landmarks.text: Radio station KTHS first broadcast from the Arlington Hotel.
landmarks.q: From which Hot Springs hotel did radio station KTHS first broadcast?
landmarks.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: KTHS Radio Station

landmarks.text: Per Wikipedia, Hot Springs declared a city holiday for Oaklawn's first day of racing, and more than 3,000 people attended.
landmarks.q: What did Hot Springs declare for Oaklawn's first day of racing, per Wikipedia?

landmarks.text: The first Arkansas Derby ran at Oaklawn Park in 1936 with a purse of $5,000.
landmarks.q: What was the purse of the first Arkansas Derby at Oaklawn in 1936?

landmarks.text: Wikipedia says the Oaklawn meet, held December through May, is sometimes called the "Fifth Season".
landmarks.q: Which Hot Springs racetrack's winter-spring meet is sometimes called the "Fifth Season"?

landmarks.text: Voters approved Amendment 100 in 2018, and Oaklawn became a full casino on April 1, 2019.
landmarks.q: Which Arkansas constitutional amendment let Oaklawn open a full casino in 2019?

landmarks.text: Arkansas Power & Light developed Lake Hamilton; Carpenter Dam, a concrete gravity dam, was completed in 1931 and the lake was created in 1932.
landmarks.q: Which dam formed Lake Hamilton, and when was it completed?

landmarks.text: Wikipedia gives Lake Hamilton as about 7,200 acres; Lake Catherine, the smaller of the two lakes, is about 1,940 acres.
landmarks.q: About how many acres is Lake Hamilton?

landmarks.text: Lake Hamilton is named for Hamilton Moses, an Arkansas Power & Light executive; Carpenter Dam is named for Flavius Josephus Carpenter.
landmarks.q: Lake Hamilton near Hot Springs is named for which Arkansas Power & Light executive?

landmarks.text: After Arkansas outlawed gambling in 1913, the Ohio Club on Central Avenue posed as the Ohio Cigar Store. A false wall hid the real club behind it.
landmarks.q: When gambling was banned, the Ohio Club on Central Avenue officially became what front business, complete with a fake wall?

landmarks.text: According to Wikipedia, a Hot Springs casino revival during Gov. Orval Faubus's administration (1955-1967) was ended in 1967 by Republican Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller.
landmarks.q: According to Wikipedia, in what year did Gov. Winthrop Rockefeller end Hot Springs' casino revival?

nature.text: Both families are real neighbors: the park's species list counts the eastern gray squirrel as present and the fox squirrel as probably present.
nature.source: NPS NPSpecies, Hot Springs National Park mammals

nature.text: Fox squirrels are the bigger cousins: about 1½–2 lb in Arkansas, while gray squirrels weigh just over a pound.
A squirrel's leaf nest sits about 40 feet up, is 12–20 inches across, and can be built in under 12 hours.
Gray squirrels bury nuts one at a time and never find them all, so they plant new trees every fall.
Oak and hickory nuts in the region fall in September and October. Red-oak acorns take two years to ripen; white oak acorns take one.
nature.source: Missouri Department of Conservation tree guide

nature.text: Squirrels snip shortleaf pine cones and eat the seeds before the cones even open.
nature.source: USDA Forest Service, Silvics of North America

nature.text: Hedge apples (Osage-orange) are native to the Red River country of Oklahoma, Texas and Arkansas. Squirrels tear them open for the seeds.
Sweetgum "gumballs" aren't nuts: they are spiky 1–1½ inch seed balls that ripen in fall and hang on all winter.
The Ozark chinquapin still grows in the park but is rare: chestnut blight reached it by 1940, and volunteers now breed blight-resistant trees.
In fall, hickories turn golden yellow and sweetgums go red, orange, maroon and purple.
Redbuds bloom pink to reddish purple from March before their leaves come out; flowering dogwood follows with white bracts.
nature.source: USDA Forest Service, Silvics of North America

nature.text: Hot Springs breezes are gentle: at Memorial Field the wind averages about 5 mph and blows from the east more than any other direction (2016–2025 records).
Every bird that flies over these battles is on Hot Springs National Park's species list, from chimney swifts to bald eagles.
nature.source: NPS NPSpecies, Hot Springs National Park birds

nature.text: A blue jay can carry five acorns at once and bury up to 5,000 in a season, but finds only about one in four, so jays plant oak trees.
nature.source: National Park Service, Species Spotlight: Oaks

nature.text: Turkey vultures ride rising warm air, holding their wings in a shallow V and tilting side to side. Their wings span about 70 inches.
Chimney swifts look like flying cigars and catch insects on the wing. They arrive in April and leave for South America in October.
Cedar waxwings travel in big, quiet flocks and eat cedar berries in winter. Look for the yellow tips on their tails.
Migrating Canada geese fly in V-shaped chevrons, and the males call a long, loud "a-honk!"
Arkansas's first modern bald eagle nest was found in 1983; now about 150–160 pairs nest in the state, and winter is the best time to spot one.
